body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#101 — filed by @domenic (2021-04), from a suggestion by @dvoytenko. 14 comments, active to 2024-08.

---

Extending `<a>` (and possibly `<area>`) with capabilities matching `navigation.navigate()`. Two straightforward pieces:

- **`replace`** — a boolean attribute making the navigation a replacement.
- **`navigateinfo`** — a string used as the `info` property of the corresponding `navigate` event. (String-only, since non-string values don't fit the attribute model.)

More speculative: allowing an `<a>` to traverse to a specific entry by `key`. That's harder — keys are runtime values, so a plain `<a key="...">` would require script to populate it anyway, which undercuts the declarative benefit.

The `replace` attribute in particular is a long-standing gap: it's currently impossible to express "this link replaces the current entry" declaratively, so apps must intercept and re-issue, losing the benefits of a real link.

Converse of WICG/navigation-api#82 (extending `navigate()` to match `<a>`/`<form>` capabilities), migrated separately.

cc @domenic @dvoytenko
